title: Oscar and the Songbook
premise: Lena Eriksen inherited her late father's vineyard with its debts intact, and the only way to keep it is to convince her estranged family she's settled and thriving. When she hires Oscar, a bakery tenant on her own land facing eviction, to pose as her boyfriend at a family reunion, their fake romance becomes the cover she needs and the truth she can't control. As the lease deadline and a predatory buyer close in, Lena uncovers that her father's will hid a second songbook of debts owed to him — leverage that could save them both if she claims it. In the end, Lena says the rehearsed sentence aloud, chooses Oscar over the inheritance, and they rebuild the vineyard together on terms of their own making.
about_author: Y. M. Ashgrove is a former sommelier turned novelist who writes romances set in places where land, money, and memory tangle. They live in a converted farmhouse with a dog named after a grape varietal and a stubborn belief that dessert is where truth comes out.

chapters.title: Debts Instead of Grapes
chapters.summary: Lena's POV opens on the failing vineyard, a foreclosure letter, and her father's will that left her liabilities dressed as legacy. Her sister calls: the family reunion is non-negotiable, and Lena must arrive with proof of a stable life. Emotional beat: dread sharpened into resolve — Lena decides the heart is a muscle she can train.

chapters.title: The Man at Table Six
chapters.summary: Still Lena's POV: she escapes a bank meeting to the bakery on her own leased land and meets Oscar, who flirts like it costs him nothing and bakes like it costs him everything. She learns his lease expires in ninety days — hers to renew or terminate. Emotional beat: inconvenient warmth she files under 'transaction.'

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Lena proposes the fake-dating arrangement: she'll renew his lease if he plays devoted boyfriend at the reunion. Oscar counters with a clause — no lying about the past, only the present. Dual POV as both rehearse their story and both notice the rehearsal feels easy. Emotional beat: a contract signed with shaking hands.

chapters.title: Reunion, First Course
chapters.summary: The family estate, Lena's POV: her sister's scrutiny, her mother's cold inventory of Lena's failures, and Oscar performing the boyfriend role so well it stings. A cousin's innocent question about the vineyard's finances nearly cracks her cover. Emotional beat: the performance working too well — by dessert she's pulled straight into it.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Keeps
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV: hiding in the wine cellar after dessert, Lena confesses a decade-old rehearsed sentence she's never said aloud — the apology that could reconcile her family. Oscar, recognizing his own buried secret in hers, shares a fragment of his. Emotional beat: intimacy by accident, both pretending it's still acting.

chapters.title: The Buyer's Offer
chapters.summary: Lena's POV: a development group offers to buy her debt and the land, promising freedom at the cost of the bakery's eviction and her father's name. Her sister, suspicious of Oscar's sudden appearance, digs into his history. Emotional beat: pressure from every side, and the first lie between Lena and Oscar — a lie of omission.

chapters.title: Songbook
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV: renovating the bakery's back room, he finds her father's hidden second songbook — a ledger of favors and debts owed to the old man, including one signed by the buyer's founder. He brings it to Lena, who must decide whether justice outside the law is inheritance enough. Emotional beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Lena's POV: she confronts the buyer with the songbook and negotiates — the debt restructured, the bakery lease protected — but the family discovers the fake-dating contract first. Her sister's betrayal and her mother's verdict land at once. Oscar, hearing she called it 'just business,' walks. Emotional beat: everything won and everything lost in a single afternoon.

chapters.title: Closing Time
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV: the bakery's final week; he boxes the ovens and refuses to return Lena's calls, convinced he was a line item. Lena arrives at closing time, not with the contract or the apology she rehearsed for a decade, but with the real sentence — said aloud, unrehearsed, about her father, her sister, and him. Emotional beat: the muscle of the heart, finally trained.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Dual POV, a season later: the vineyard runs as a cooperative under the restructured terms, the bakery thrives, and the family reunion comes to them this year — awkward, imperfect, real. Lena and Oscar press their first joint vintage and argue happily over what to name it. Emotional beat: quiet, earned joy; identity chosen, not inherited.
